title: Run goroutines that may panic
prompt:
Write `RunAll(fns ...func()) []error`.

- Run every function in its own goroutine, all at the same time, and wait for all of them.
- A panic must not crash the program: `errs[i]` is an error whose message contains the panic value; functions that return normally get `nil`.

`RunAll(ok, func() { panic(123) })` → `[nil, "panic: 123"]`.
hint: `recover` only works in the panicking goroutine, so each goroutine needs its own deferred `recover` that writes `errs[i]`.
